info.album: Ain't No Stoppin' Us Now (The Eric Kupper Remixes)

podcast.body: This song achieved the number one position on the Billboard R&B chart and reached number 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1979. While Kenny Gamble presented it as a message to the Black community, its writers, McFadden and Whitehead, understood it as a declaration of their independence from Gamble and PIR's creative directives, a viewpoint that diverged from the company's perceived political focus. "Ain't No Stop and Us Now. McFadden and Whitehead, number one billboard R&D chart, number 13 billboard Hot 179."

srcs.episode: Ep. 37 - Philly Soul and the Sound of the 70s

podcast.body: This song was preferred by Pittsburgh Pirates player Dave Parker over "We Are Family" as a team anthem in 1979. "Dave Parker was not so sure about we are family. He preferred ain't no stop in us now, but Willie Stargel was the leader of that team."
